description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/filenode.rs:849-1248 (handle_filenode_copy).

RFC 8620 §5.4 defines the standard `Foo/copy` method shape. Among the
top-level arguments it mandates:

- `onSuccessDestroyOriginal: Boolean` (default false). "If true, an
  attempt will be made to destroy the original records that were
  successfully copied: after emitting the Foo/copy response, but
  before processing the next method, the server MUST make a single
  call to Foo/set to destroy the original of each successfully
  copied record."
- `destroyFromIfInState: String|null`. Passed as `ifInState` to the
  implicit Foo/set call when destroying the originals.

draft-ietf-jmap-filenode-13 §3.2.4 says "This is a standard Foo/copy
function with the same additional top-level arguments as FileNode/set,
onDestroyRemoveChildren and onExists, with the same behaviour." The
"standard Foo/copy" wording incorporates the RFC 8620 §5.4 contract by
reference, including the two arguments above.

Current handler behaviour:

- `onSuccessDestroyOriginal` is never read from `args`. A client that
  sends `{ ..., "onSuccessDestroyOriginal": true }` gets the source
  records LEFT IN PLACE despite the spec MUST. The client believes
  the move was atomic-ish; the originals leak.
- `destroyFromIfInState` is never read. Even if a consumer manually
  wired an implicit Foo/set destroy as a follow-up `Invocation`,
  there is no path to forward the from-side state guard.

Concrete failure mode: a client uses FileNode/copy with
`onSuccessDestroyOriginal: true` to move a node from account A to
account B. The handler ignores the flag, so the node exists in both
accounts. Subsequent FileNode/changes calls on account A do not show
the node as destroyed because it never was. The client either
double-handles or silently leaks N source records per Foo/copy call.

Required fix:

1. Parse both args from the request envelope.
2. When `onSuccessDestroyOriginal=true`, emit a follow-up `Invocation`
   into the returned `tail` Vec carrying `FileNode/set` with `destroy:
   [<successfully-copied-source-ids>]` and `ifInState:
   destroyFromIfInState` (the per-RFC mandate to issue the
   destruction as a real method call, not internally). The dispatcher
   then processes that invocation as part of the same request.
3. Document that the destroy is server-emitted (not client-emitted)
   so consumers' middleware doesn't double-count.

Risk: this is a real interop hazard. Any client built against the
JMAP spec expects `onSuccessDestroyOriginal` to work; the current
silent-ignore is a wire-protocol compliance gap.

LABELS: api-contract, underspecified, spec
title: handle_filenode_copy ignores onSuccessDestroyOriginal and destroyFromIfInState (RFC 8620 §5.4 standard Foo/copy args)
